title: Treaty of Shimoda
text: The Treaty of Shimoda , formally the Treaty of Commerce and Navigation between Japan and Russia , was the first treaty between the Russian Empire and the Empire of Japan, signed on February 7, 1855. Signed shortly after the Convention of Kanagawa between Japan and the United States, it effectively meant the end of Japan's 220-year-old policy of national seclusion (sakoku) by opening the ports of Nagasaki, Shimoda and Hakodate to Russian vessels. The treaty also established the position of Russian consuls in Japan and defined the borders between Japan and Russia.
